newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts pay tribute to Ericsson mobile growth.
newsitem.headline: Analysts pay tribute to Ericsson mobile growth.

text.p: Swedish analysts paid tribute on Friday to a 100 percent rise in L.M. Ericsson AB's mobile phone sales in the first quarter of 1997.

The analysts, declining to be named before an analysts' conference call with Ericsson management beginning at 1500 GMT, said the 30 percent rise in pre-tax profit was a welcome relief for the Swedish market after disappointments from drug majors Astra and Pharmacia & Upjohn earlier this week.
"As for the minuses I would point to the company's negative cashflow and somewhat weaker sales of mobile systems," one analyst said.
Ericsson dipped in late Stockholm trading, falling 2.0 crowns to 250.5 crowns in heavy trading of over 1.0 billion crowns.

"I think many had expected a worse result after Astra's disappointment. On this weak market it's a sign of strength that Ericsson's share held itself steady, especially after a strong rise on Thursday," said another analyst.
"We think the profit was good, well up to expectations, but it is the foreigners who are selling now and pushing the price down," said a Stockholm broker.
Pre-tax profit for the first quarter totalled 2.02 billion crowns compared to market expectations of 1.99 billion.
